background: Bank of Scotland plc is one of the ring-fenced banks of Lloyds Banking Group, trading as Bank of Scotland and Halifax, funded by UK retail deposits and lending mainly on residential mortgages.
synthesis: Bank of Scotland is rated AA- on average across all three main agencies, the weakest of them at A+, all three on a stable outlook, after a one-notch upgrade by one of the three on 12 May 2026. Capital is mixed against UK majors, CET1 of 14.1% above the peer median but leverage of 4.5% in the bottom quarter, which is the figure to watch; liquidity is similar, LCR of 144% above the median and NSFR of 123% below it. Since 30 Jun 2024 CET1 has risen 0.7 points while leverage, LCR and NSFR have been broadly flat (figures to 30 Jun 2026). The newest flagged item, on 2 Oct 2026, is an online banking outage shared across the group's brands, operational rather than credit news, with a large cost-cutting plan and higher group profits before it.
